title: Etale locality on the source plus smooth locality on the target implies locality on the source-and-target
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a property of morphisms which is etale local on the source, smooth local on the target and stable under postcomposition with open immersions is local on the source-and-target for the etale square condition (statement lines 7903-7932). The proof has several genuinely different stages. It first uses etale locality on the source to reduce to the case of a cartesian diagram (proof lines 7934-7938), then one direction follows from smooth locality on the target (proof lines 7940-7943). The converse is the hard part: after replacing the target by a smooth neighbourhood one reduces to the case where the target is etale over an affine space, obtains a commutative cube, and reduces the claim to exhibiting a specific open subscheme of affine space which meets every fibre; the author explicitly remarks that the naive translation-invariance argument requires extra etale localization on the target and is annoying, and instead uses the automorphisms from the group action lemma together with the case n = 1 reduction to exclude a finite exceptional set, and finally kills the remaining characteristic p possibility with the Artin-Schreier style map sending coordinates to their difference with their p-th powers, whose etaleness is checked by differentiating (proof lines 7945-8039). The claim is H3: a multi-stage reduction with an explicit strategic choice inside it and a genuinely original final step.
